summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for failure to thrive and significant weight loss following a recent hospitalization for post-ERCP pancreatitis. She reported poor oral intake, early satiety, nausea, and difficulty maintaining nutrition at home. During admission, her oral intake improved with dietary modifications, including a switch to clear Nepro supplements, and calorie counts confirmed adequate intake. Her weight stabilized at 42 kg. A subtherapeutic INR of 1.1 was identified, prompting initiation of a heparin drip to bridge anticoagulation until warfarin achieved a therapeutic INR of 1.6. Orthostatic hypotension led to a temporary hold and subsequent dose reduction of labetalol. She remained on home medications including lamotrigine, omeprazole, and trazodone, with no psychiatric medication changes. Hemodialysis was continued throughout the stay. Discharge planning included warfarin dose adjustment, INR monitoring at dialysis, daily weight checks, and coordination with elder services for grocery assistance. She was discharged home in stable condition with improved nutrition and therapeutic anticoagulation.
